- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to recent highs.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion or short-term rebound.
- Avoid overreacting to recent spikes — if price spiked >5% in last 3 days, cap forecast increase to 2–4% to prevent overshoot.
- Lagged corrections: if true outcome is lower than forecast by >2% over 3–5 days, adjust next forecast downward by 0.5–1.5%.
- For 30-day horizon, reduce forecast sensitivity to sentiment extremes — sentiment >0.8 or <0.2 should trigger a 1–2% downward adjustment to avoid overfitting.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 14-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals without sentiment confirmation — if sentiment drops below 0.2, don’t assume immediate price drop unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive low sentiment days.
